speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing weakness and fatigue; to help me identify the cause, could you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you have noticed any other changes in your health?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds exhausting. To help narrow this down, are you experiencing specific symptoms like muscle aches, dark urine, or fever alongside this fatigue? Also, do you have any known history of thyroid issues or autoimmune diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the update. The presence of mild diplopia (double vision) alongside progressive weakness is concerning for a neuromuscular issue like Myasthenia Gravis. Do you notice these symptoms worsen significantly after physical activity or toward the end of the day, and do you experience any trouble swallowing or breathing?

REQUEST TEST: Creatine_Phosphokinase (CK)
REQUEST TEST: Thyroid_Stimulating_Hormone (TSH)

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis

The normal creatine kinase and thyroid levels effectively rule out myositis and thyroid storm, leaving the neuromuscular junction as the primary suspect given your progressive weakness and diplopia. Since these symptoms often worsen with activity and improve with rest, has your weakness noticeably increased after prolonged physical exertion or standing? Additionally, have you experienced any difficulty swallowing food or liquids, or any sensation of choking?
